assets.prompt: One isolated slender curved robot kitten tail on a transparent background. Warm matte ivory, subtle charcoal joints, tiny amber tip, soft cinematic shading, no black outline or alternating stripes.

notes: Desktop and phone each use one complete plate and projection. There is no split sky extension.
Clouds, creek reflections and waterfall highlights animate through registered GPU texture displacement, under one gently moving camera.
Original hero-bg.mp4 supplies only upper crops (desktop y=0..400, phone x=360..920/y=0..300), masked to the sky. Its observer and equipment are never sampled.
Small JPEG robot plates provide matching fallback compositions; a cropped night-sky image handles unavailable video.
Weather is a deterministic aesthetic cycle, not a forecast. Browser-local time controls the six phases.
Wetness, stream runoff and waterfall flow retain separate response times. OS/user reduced motion and offscreen pause are respected.
Night vegetation has a separate warm emission/bloom pass, applied after night exposure and before fog/rain, with a static fallback.
Only the nearest 14% of the photographic plate receives a softly feathered breeze displacement. Distant meadow and slope vegetation, robot and kitten remain still.
Companion amber components are identified by their native color inside tiny registered component footprints. No silhouette mask or dark oval is applied.
Sunset relights the existing cloud texture in violet, coral, orange and gold. The old night sky is suppressed during sunset and returns later.
Robot and kitten indicator lights have separate soft double-blink schedules. A dedicated role texture isolates these pulses from the luminous meadow.
Reduced motion fixes the tail at rest and the indicator lights at steady brightness.
The camera projection is now fixed at all times. Cloud drift frequency is increased about 2.4 times, with the same bounded displacement and terrain-safe distance field.
The independent transparent tail sprite replaces the outlined procedural tail; its occasional gesture and tip light follow the existing attachment point.
Terrain, stream and waterfall use the same sunset grading. Waterfall animation modulates photographed foam and excludes dark border rocks instead of adding a blue-white ribbon.
Dreamcore rendering resolves fine terrain texture once in a registered Canvas plate; sky, waterfall, stream and companions are preserved. No new scene geometry or camera motion.
Nocturnal meadow emission uses multi-scale continuous light pools in lilac and mint, instead of sharp flower-tip points. Device amber cores retain separate blink channels.
Broad low-contrast valley air and diffuse creek glints reduce hard microcontrast; this styling also has a static Canvas fallback.
